title: Immunization Protocol Clause 4 — One Influenza Choice per Season and Doses at One Visit
content:
**4.1 One influenza choice per season.** The two influenza vaccinations of Immunization Services are one choice per season: a patient never holds a Seasonal Influenza Standard-Dose Vaccination course and a Seasonal Influenza High-Dose Vaccination course for the same season.

**4.2 Patients aged 65 or older.** A patient aged 65 or older is offered the high-dose course; the standard-dose course is given to such a patient only as the high-dose vaccination's listed substitute when high-dose stock is out.

**4.3 Several vaccines at one visit.** Several vaccines may be given at one visit where each one is marked as allowed at the same visit as other vaccines, but no more than 4 doses per patient per day. The count is every dose given to the patient on that calendar day, across all of the patient's courses. Further doses are booked for another day.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer under clause 4 |
|---|---|
| May a patient hold both influenza courses for one season? | No; one of the two per season. |
| Which influenza course is offered to a patient aged 65 or older? | The high-dose course; the standard-dose course only as its listed substitute when high-dose stock is out. |
| How many doses may a patient receive on one calendar day? | No more than 4, counted across all of the patient's courses. |
| What happens to a dose beyond that number? | It is booked for another day. |

## Hypothetical visit counts

- A hypothetical patient has received 3 doses today across different courses; a fourth dose today is within the limit of 4.
- The same patient asking for a fifth dose today is beyond the limit; that dose is booked for another day.
